newsitem.title: UK: M&G H1 held back by UK retail business.
newsitem.headline: M&G H1 held back by UK retail business.

text.p: Fund management group M&G Group Plc said on Thursday its underperforming UK unit trust business had constrained first half profit growth to six percent.
The group said earnings were held back by relative underperformance in some of its unit trusts, but that it believed its value investment approach remained fundamentally valid.

"We think these results have demonstrated the basic resilience of the business because it is a style that has not done well...it has not been an easy environment for us," group managing director Michael McLintock told Reuters.
Pre-tax profits were 33.2 million stg from 31.2 million a year earlier, while the interim dividend was left unchanged at 16 pence.
Sales of unit trusts and Personal Equity Plans were down at 312 million stg from 558 million a year earlier.
He said that there was room for improvement in the group's investment process and fund range.
"We think the prospects for value are actually pretty good in this market but we always think there are ways we can improve," said McLintock.
He said the group had been making a number of changes, including improving communication between managers, more thorough research and freeing managers from administrative restrictions.

M&G is looking at its fund range and plans proposals to unitholders in a few months about clarifying the identity of some funds."Part of the review is looking at areas where there are gaps in the fund ranges as well as where there are overlaps," he explained.

He said institutional business had picked up since the end of the first half, with about 250 million stg in new business since the end of March, although it was difficult to predict its effect on results.

M&G also said there were early signs of a pick-up in its UK equity unit trusts. McLintock said this was evident in three of its four UK equity income funds appearing in the upper or top quartile of performance in the period.

"Usually income funds tend to foreshadow improvement more generally in our value style. We are making our judgement on prospects for value style in terms of the relative value of the shares that we hold. We think that many of the shares that we hold are just too cheap."

He said the group was getting about 300 applications a day for windfall PEP business and while there was little initial boost to profits, there would be new customers to whom it could market the M&G product.

He said there was no significance about leaving the dividend unchanged. "Our results remain very dependent as a fund management business on market levels and on relative performance and we have still got the best part of 4-1/2 months to the end of the year.
There were good prospects on the institutional side as well as international opportunities, but this would not distract from the need to refocus the local product.
He said the group was wary about acquisitions in a people oriented business, but wouldn't rule out international arrangements if they suited M&G, such as reciprocal fund management arrangements.

M&G has funds under management of some 16.1 billion sterling, up six percent on a year earlier. About 70 percent of this is in the UK, seven to eight percent in fixed interest and the balance international.
About a third of funds under management are institutional.
